truth: Hammerfell is a hot, dry land of desert, rock and sea. The Redguards came to it from sunken Yokuda: first a wave of warriors who took the land by the sword, then the royal court that followed. Their descendants are the Forebears and the Crowns, still divided over tradition, trade and the Empire. Water decides everything. Oases and wells belong to Crown families and desert tribes, the ports belong to Forebear merchant houses, and the caravan roads pay them both. Swords are a calling and the dead are honoured in great necropolises, so necromancers are hated above every other criminal. In the last war the Empire gave Hammerfell's land to the Dominion, and Hammerfell won it back alone.

sentinel.truth: A capital of domes on a harbour cliff, ruling a coast of palm scrub and terraced gardens and a desert hinterland of salt flats. Sentinel's wealth is dye, spice and the end of the Alik'r caravan road. The king holds the cisterns, so he holds the city. The court is split between Crown nobles in the palace and Forebear merchants on the quays, and the Betony claim against Daggerfall is a weapon both sides use. The coast fiefs to the south-west are harpy country, and the Witches of the Marsh rule the reeds of Tigonus.

alikr_desert.truth: The heart of Hammerfell: a sea of dunes, gravel plains and red mesas. Wealth runs through wells along the caravan road, and every well is owned. Crown families hold the great oases, nomad tribes hold the hidden wells, and caravans pay both. Berbaaqnia is a walled caravanserai city. The hot Dak'fron plain has old dragon dens that were empty for an age and are not empty now. Under the sand lie Yokudan tombs, a buried royal city and a Dwemer hall half full of drift.

bangkorai.truth: The only green, wet corner of Hammerfell: red-clay river valleys under jungle at the bay head, with mountain fiefs above them. River ports trade timber, fish and cargo from the Bjoulsae bridge, and their towns are tavern-crowded and half Breton in manner. Totambu carries the name of the old royal line, which makes it sacred to the Crowns. Its timber lords and the Order of the Scarab are pushing into groves where giants live. Orc bands left over from old wars hold strongholds in the hills. The old Bangkorai pass, with its garrison, still guards the land road between High Rock and Hammerfell.

dragontail.truth: The mountain wall between Hammerfell and Cyrodiil: black volcanic ridges in the north, red rock and slot canyons in the south. Its ore and obsidian arm every swordsmith in the province, and its miners are bound by debt to the lords of Dragontail city, a terraced town of black stone. Fumaroles steam in the high valleys, and fire spirits walk in the lava tubes. The Devilrock witches trade fire-pacts. Scourg Barrow, the greatest tomb in the mountains, is said to be waking.

stros_mkai.truth: A small, two-lobed island in the southern sea. A harbour town (Port Hunding) climbs the east side of a south-facing bay toward a walled palace plateau, and a high western plateau holds a Dwemer ruin. Both treaties that bound Hammerfell to the Empire were signed here: the first after the Crowns lost at Hunding Bay, the second after Hammerfell beat the Dominion. That makes the island neutral ground that both Crowns and Forebears covet. Smugglers use the cave behind the waterfall. A necromancer's tower stands on an islet off the north-west coast, and the islanders do not row there.

craglorn.truth: Craglorn is a high, dry tableland of red badlands, wind-carved spires and star-fall craters wedged between the Dragontail Mountains, Bangkorai and Skyrim's Falkreath pass. In the east, Elinhir climbs granite tiers as a city of mages, star-watchers and stone-cutters; in the north-west, Dragonstar rings its famous gladiator arena inside a border fort. Long before the Redguards landed, Nedic star-cults built observatories and vaulted bastions into the crags, and fallen sky-shards still fuse the sand into eerie glass. Today arena patrons fix fights in Dragonstar while serpents and Celestial cultists stir in the ancient pinnacles.

hews_bane.truth: Hew's Bane is a sun-baked peninsula of limestone headlands, sea arches and sheltered coves on the southern Abecean coast. Taneth rises in cliff-palace terraces above a wealthy harbour, while Abah's Landing crowds a stilt-pier cove where merchant syndicates and the Thieves Guild share the docks. During the Great War, Taneth fell to the Aldmeri Dominion after traitors opened its gates; twenty years later, the city is rebuilding through sea trade, but Alik'r hunters still track the remaining collaborators from Hammerfell to Skyrim. Ancient Yokudan necropolises and flooded slave-coves line the cliffs beyond the terraced pool gardens.
